A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FiFA research and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SD1.5 and SDXL experiments, automatic evaluations in Table 1, human evaluations in Figure 4, and component, safety, and training analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds three experiments in Appendix K and Figure 14.

M1.justification: FiFA's margin, LLM text-quality, diversity scoring, and top-K selection procedure remain unchanged. ImageReward tests another reward-model choice within the existing framework; suggested online-DPO applications remain future-work discussion.

E1.justification: Appendix K adds a targeted training scenario enriched in duplicated or similar Pick-a-Pic v2 prompts, changing the represented prompt distribution. The main training datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and text-to-image tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their baseline membership. Figure 14c reuses full-dataset training and random selection; ImageReward serves as a scoring and evaluation function, rather than a new competing filtering method.

E3.justification: New experiments select prompts repeated more than 20 times or sharing keywords, vary diversity weights, exclude the highest-margin 10% of pairs, and use ImageReward for selection and evaluation. These add controlled protocols without revising the retained experiments' settings.

E4.justification: Appendix K and Figure 14 add targeted tests of diversity under prompt redundancy, dependence on the highest-margin pairs, and robustness to reward-model choice. These extend the existing component, hyperparameter, and reward-weighted-loss analyses.

E5.justification: Seed and statistical reporting practices remain unchanged, including Appendix D's generation seeds 0–199. The added Figure 14 curves introduce no repeated-run counts, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 and existing figure results are unchanged. New Figure 14 reports better PickScore with diversity weighting under repetitive prompts, reduced performance after excluding the highest-margin pairs, and higher ImageReward for FiFA than full-data or random-selection training.

T1.justification: The selection objective, entropy approximation, G-optimal-design theorem, linear-noise assumption, and derivations in Appendices B and I remain substantively unchanged. Added equation numbers and updated references do not introduce new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims about automated filtering, efficient alignment, human preference, and safety. The reported 17% human-preference advantage and data/computation savings claims remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the added tests as showing particular benefits of diversity in repetitive datasets and informative signals from the highest-margin pairs. Section 4.3 clarifies the margin-versus-diversity tradeoff, and the limitations discussion proposes specific online-DPO and policy-gradient extensions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a project-page link and construction criteria for the new experimental subsets. Appendix A's implementation settings remain unchanged, while Section 4.1 removes the explicit tie-exclusion and training-image provenance descriptions.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds LIMA by Zhou et al. and SeRA by Ko et al., explicitly connecting FiFA to implicit-reward-margin selection for LLM alignment. The broader positioning and other cited works remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized prose edits, expands limitations, updates publication and acknowledgment text, and inserts a new results appendix. Related work and additional examples shift from Appendices K/L to L/M; the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the three-panel Figure 14, relocates Figure 5 from page 9 to page 8, and clarifies Table 1's caption. Existing graphical content is retained, with subsequent example figures renumbered and surrounding text reflowed.

improvement.justification: Appendix K and Figure 14 strengthen empirical support for diversity and high-margin selection and extend validation to ImageReward, while preserving the main results. Expanded limitations and related work improve context. The gains are modest: the new experiments provide limited reproducibility detail and no uncertainty estimates, and some dataset provenance information is removed.
